newsitem.title: UK: Shaky London gold slides lower, eyes downside.
newsitem.headline: Shaky London gold slides lower, eyes downside.

text.p: Gold traded nervously on the verge of fresh 3-1/4 year lows on Thursday, and dealers said prices were poised to extend the slide they began last year.
"Gold keeps looking like its going to crack. But it's getting good physical demand from the Middle and Far East which is keeping it around $343.00," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $342.80 and ounce, a fresh low since September 14, 1993, and down from the morning's fixing of $343.40. Prices were tr
Dealers and analysts are looking for prices to sink to around $340 an ounce, a key low area, in the very near future.
In contrast, the price of palladium marched briskly higher as deepening concern about delayed Russian supplies put a bullish spin on the market, dealers said.
Palladium was fixed at $129.00 an ounce in the afternoon, up $1.50 from the morning and the highest level in six months.

Dealers said palladium, an industrial metal used in electronics, auto catalytic converters and dentistry, showed upside potential as long as major producer Russia and Japanese consumers failed to clinch sales agreements for the year.
"Palladium is becoming well sought after. Not only do you have the consumers in the market, but fund interest is coming in," a dealer noted.
Gold's sliding prices, which have declined by some $25 an ounce since the start of the year, have boosted demand in the Middle East and Asia, according to the World Gold Council.
But physical offtake has been unable to offset the market's overwhelmingly bearish tone, deepened by fears that central banks will continue selling their reserves this year.
Fresh institutional selling last week was attributed by some dealers to a central bank, although others have pointed the finger at gold producers panicking about gold's steep decline.
More producer hedging was feared as the gold price in South African rand and Australian dollars fell to fresh lows. Continued strength in the dollar was also expected to limit fresh investment.
Technical analysts noted that gold may need to consolidate after sinking to fresh 3-1/4 year lows earlier this week.
But any move higher would stall at $346-$347, they added.
Silver was two cents easier at $4.82/$4.84 compared to Wednesday's London close. It was expected to remain in a $4.80-$5.00 range for the time being.
Platinum was up $1.00 at $351.25/$352.25, with palladium.
